sources.entry: Peergos - Secure and private space online where you can store, share and view your photos, videos, music and documents. Also includes a calendar, news feed, task lists, chat and email client. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Java

summary.one_liner: Peergos is a peer-to-peer, end-to-end encrypted personal storage and social platform with file sharing, a messenger, and an email client, which can be self-hosted.
summary.what_it_does: Peergos provides an encrypted global filesystem built on IPFS, where each file is encrypted on the user's machine in 5MiB chunks before storage. Users can share files with other users or via secret links whose key material stays in the browser and is not sent to the server. The README also describes a secure messenger, an encrypted email client and bridge, a social network built on a friend-request model, and a calendar and other web apps. Users can run a Peergos daemon on their own machine or home server, sign up with a token, and sync folders with a bi-directional sync client. Other access routes include a FUSE mount, a WebDAV bridge, a CLI shell, and S3 or Postgres storage backends for self-hosted servers.
use_cases: share files with friends without exposing metadata
sync a local folder with a private cloud
mount cloud storage as a local drive or WebDAV share
how_to_run: Install Java 25 or newer (or use the native packages)
Open the localhost signup link printed by the daemon and create an account with the token
For LAN access: java -jar Peergos.jar daemon -generate-token true -listen-host 0.0.0.0
Build from source: ant dist (requires jdk17 and ant, per the Development section)
notable: Client-side encryption with separate keys per file or directory; explicitly not convergent encryption
Login derives keys from username and password via scrypt so keys never leave the client
Friend requests are cryptographically blinded so the server cannot see who follows whom
Can be self-hosted, mirrored, or migrated to another server while keeping the same identity
Cryptree-based access control adapted from Wuala, extended to hide file names, sizes and structure
caveats: Requires Java 25 or newer to run the jar; builds need jdk17 and ant
Peergos does not provide anonymity yet, according to the README; Tor is suggested as a workaround
Browsers only allow apps and large downloads on https or localhost, so a domain with TLS is needed for remote web access
Files shared between users are described as vulnerable to a sufficiently large quantum computer until a post-quantum asymmetric scheme is adopted
Minio has issues with the S3 settings, so the README recommends turning off some options for it
